deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: This setting controls whether the node group can be deleted. Preventing accidental deletion helps keep important infrastructure available.

description.description: An optional textual description of the resource.
description.rationale: This field is only used to describe the node group. Changing the description does not affect how the resource works or how secure it is.

initial_size.description: The initial number of nodes in the node group. One of 'initial_size' or 'autoscaling_policy' must be configured on resource creation.
initial_size.rationale: This field sets how many nodes are created when the group is first set up. The right number depends on the workload, so there is no single secure value for every environment.

maintenance_policy.description: Specifies how to handle instances when a node in the group undergoes maintenance. Set to one of: DEFAULT, RESTART_IN_PLACE, or MIGRATE_WITHIN_NODE_GROUP. The default value is DEFAULT.
maintenance_policy.rationale: This field decides how the node group handles planned maintenance. Different options suit different workloads, so there is no single security setting that is right for everyone.

name.rationale: This field is only used to identify the node group. Changing its name does not change how the resource is protected.

node_template.description: The URL of the node template to which this node group belongs.
node_template.rationale: This field identifies the node template used by the group. The correct template depends on the organisation's infrastructure, so there is no single security value that applies to everyone.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: This field identifies which Google Cloud project the node group belongs to. It does not change the security settings of the node group by itself.

zone.description: Zone where this node group is located
zone.rationale: Determines the region/zone where the resource is created. Policy should restrict it to an approved-region whitelist for data residency; the allowed set is parameterised (a hardcoded example whitelist is acceptable).

autoscaling_policy.description:
If you use sole-tenant nodes for your workloads, you can use the node
group autoscaler to automatically manage the sizes of your node groups.

One of 'initial_size' or 'autoscaling_policy' must be configured on resource creation.

autoscaling_policy.max_nodes.description:
Maximum size of the node group. Set to a value less than or equal
to 100 and greater than or equal to min-nodes.
autoscaling_policy.max_nodes.rationale: This field sets the largest size the node group can grow to. The right limit depends on the workload and available capacity, so there is no single secure value for every environment.

autoscaling_policy.min_nodes.description:
Minimum size of the node group. Must be less
than or equal to max-nodes. The default value is 0.
autoscaling_policy.min_nodes.rationale: This field sets the smallest size the node group can shrink to. The right number depends on the workload, so there is no single secure value for every environment.

autoscaling_policy.mode.description:
The autoscaling mode. Set to one of the following:
  - OFF: Disables the autoscaler.
  - ON: Enables scaling in and scaling out.
  - ONLY_SCALE_OUT: Enables only scaling out.
  You must use this mode if your node groups are configured to
  restart their hosted VMs on minimal servers. Possible values: ["OFF", "ON", "ONLY_SCALE_OUT"]
autoscaling_policy.mode.rationale: This field controls whether the node group grows or shrinks automatically. The correct mode depends on how the service is operated, so there is no single secure option for every environment.

maintenance_window.description: contains properties for the timeframe of maintenance

maintenance_window.start_time.description: instances.start time of the window. This must be in UTC format that resolves to one of 00:00, 04:00, 08:00, 12:00, 16:00, or 20:00. For example, both 13:00-5 and 08:00 are valid.
maintenance_window.start_time.rationale: This field sets when planned maintenance can begin. The best time depends on the organisation's operating hours, so there is no single secure time for every environment.

share_settings.description: Share settings for the node group.

share_settings.share_type.description: Node group sharing type. Possible values: ["ORGANIZATION", "SPECIFIC_PROJECTS", "LOCAL"]
share_settings.share_type.rationale: This setting controls how widely the node group is shared. Sharing it too broadly could allow more projects to use the infrastructure than intended.

share_settings.project_map.description: A map of project id and project config. This is only valid when shareType's value is SPECIFIC_PROJECTS.

share_settings.project_map.id.rationale: This field identifies an entry in the sharing configuration. The correct value depends on the organisation's projects, so there is no single security value that applies to every environment.

share_settings.project_map.project_id.description: The project id/number should be the same as the key of this project config in the project map.
share_settings.project_map.project_id.rationale: This field identifies which project can use the shared node group. Approved project IDs are different for every organisation, so there is no universal security value for this field.
